stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dt} = 6 t + 3 y - 12 \). Without drawing it, describe the field of slope segments for this equation: where the segments are horizontal, where they have positive slope, and where they have negative slope.

answer_key.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( y = 4 - 2 t \), have positive slope where \( y > 4 - 2 t \), and have negative slope where \( y < 4 - 2 t \).

worked_solution.text: A segment is horizontal where the right side is 0: \( 6 t + 3 y - 12 = 0 \) exactly when \( y = 4 - 2 t \), which is the line \( y = 4 - 2 t \).
The right side equals \( 3\left(2 t + y - 4\right) \), so its sign is positive where \( y > 4 - 2 t \) and negative where \( y < 4 - 2 t \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the slope on each side of the locus

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( t = 4 - 2 y \), have positive slope where \( t > 4 - 2 y \), and have negative slope where \( t < 4 - 2 y \).
options.derivation: each lattice point read with its coordinates exchanged, so t and y trade places

options.label: The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( y = 4 - 2 t \), have positive slope where \( y > 4 - 2 t \), and have negative slope where \( y < 4 - 2 t \).
The segments are horizontal exactly along the line \( y = 4 \), have positive slope where \( y > 4 \), and have negative slope where \( y < 4 \).
options.derivation: the slope read as depending on y alone, the t term ignored, so the segments would match along horizontal lines

options.derivation: the horizontal row located but the tilt on each side taken from the look of a familiar field instead of from a computed slope
